42.0.0.en: 1 Then Job answered the LORD, and said, 2 I know that thou canst do every thing, and that no thought can be withholden from thee. 3 Who is he that hideth counsel without knowledge? therefore have I uttered that I understood not; things too wonderful for me, which I knew not. 4 Hear, I beseech thee, and I will speak: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.

42.0.1.en: There is no path to glory except enjoying the spirit of humility filled with love, that is, sharing in the traits of the Lord Christ, who is Love and who calls us: “Learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls” (Mt 11:29).

42.0.2.en: Then Job answered the LORD, and said: [1]

42.0.3.en: While the friends were determined that Job should confess the hidden sins that had caused him these successive disasters, and should ask God's forgiveness for them, God did not rebuke him for hidden sins. Instead He put questions to him so that he might realize his inability to examine the wisdom of God, His plan and His ordering. It was fitting for Job to trust in God's surpassing care even when He permits trials that seem unbearable.

42.0.4.en: However great man's wisdom may be, as a being subject to time he cannot comprehend the mind of God, nor come to know His purposes concerning our eternity.

42.1.0.en: I know that thou canst do every thing, and that no thought can be withholden from thee [2].

42.1.1.en: After confessing God's surpassing power, Job confessed his ignorance of God's plan, and that it would have been fitting for him to trust in Him without hesitation or question. It is as though he says to Him: “Your power has no limit and Your wisdom is absolute. Is it not fitting for me to surrender my whole life to You without dispute?!”

42.1.2.en: Truly, when trials come upon us, especially if they are heavy, sudden and successive, many questions go round in our minds, among them:

42.1.3.en: · Are these trials a chastening for certain sins? Let us examine ourselves and contemplate God our Savior, for He is the forgiver of sins and remembers them no more.

42.1.4.en: · Is it a war from Satan to destroy me? I do not fear the enemy of good and all his devices, for God has given me authority over him, and his place has become under the believer's feet.

42.1.5.en: · Is it to test me, as happened with Job? Then let me trust in the Lord Christ, who strengthens me and grants me the spirit of victory.

42.1.6.en: · Is it for reasons I do not know? Let me humble myself before God, trusting in His divine wisdom, which cannot be comprehended.

42.1.7.en: * After the Lord showed His faithful servant how strong and deceitful Leviathan, his enemy, is, Job answered on both matters, saying: [I know that thou canst do every thing]; and as for his hidden schemes he added: [and that no thought can be withholden from thee].

42.1.9.en: Who is he that hideth counsel without knowledge!

42.1.10.en: Therefore have I uttered that I understood not.

42.2.0.en: Things too wonderful for me, which I knew not [3].

42.2.1.en: This phrase is quoted from the words of Almighty God (Job 38:2), spoken to rebuke Job for the way he used in explaining God's dealings. The Lord spoke it because we often hide God's counsel or distort it by words we utter in folly...

42.2.2.en: It is as though he says: I am the man without knowledge; my sin is before me, for in ignorance I did not grasp Your divine purposes concerning the trials that have come upon me.

42.2.3.en: In true humility and remorse Job confesses that he erred in his words under the weight of the pressure of suffering, and entered into a dialogue about God's plan as an equal with an equal, though he cannot comprehend God's plan. It is as though he says to Him: “I am a man; I spoke what I did not understand; I thrust myself into wonderful divine matters that exceed my comprehension!”

42.2.4.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) sees Job criticizing Leviathan by this phrase: [Although Leviathan works in secret against those whom he tempts, he cannot hide anything from the One who defends the tempted.]

42.2.5.en: * [Therefore I have spoken foolishly, of things beyond my knowledge.] All human wisdom, however exact, is counted foolishness when compared with divine wisdom. For all just and beautiful human deeds, when compared with God's justice and beauty, are neither just nor beautiful, indeed they do not exist at all.

42.2.6.en: So although Moses had been trained in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, when he heard the Lord speaking he at once discovered that he was a hesitant man and slow of tongue, saying: [O my Lord, I am not eloquent, neither heretofore, nor since thou hast spoken unto thy servant: but I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue] (Ex 4:10)... So also Jeremiah, when he heard God's words, found he had no words to speak, for he says: “Ah, Lord GOD! behold, I cannot speak: for I am a child” (Jer 1:6)...

42.2.7.en: See, the more Job rebuked himself, the more he advanced, and he believed that his knowledge had increased beyond measure, because he perceived in the Lord's words the mysteries of His wisdom, beyond his imagining.

42.2.9.en: Hear, I beseech thee, and I will speak.

42.3.0.en: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me [4].

42.3.1.en: Job no longer speaks in order to protest against what has befallen him, but in humility he pleads that God would reveal His wisdom to him, for he longs to learn.

42.3.2.en: Job's tone has changed. He no longer converses with God as one who knows everything, but confesses that he needs God Himself to explain to him what he does not comprehend. He does not cease to ask so that the Lord may give him understanding. In humility he asks to come to know the divine truth.

42.3.3.en: The Hebrew word “al’shaa, ask” carries a deep humility and a serious desire to learn. He pleads with Him to teach him.

42.3.4.en: Job no longer asks to enter into dialogue and dispute with God, but asks that He permit him to sit at His feet and learn from Him what His incomprehensible divine ways are.

42.3.5.en: * “Hearing,” for us, means preparing our ear in one place to hear a voice coming from another place. But for God, in whom there is nothing external, hearing means that He looks upon our longings that rise to Him from below. For us, speaking with God, who knows the hearts even of those who are silent, is not uttering words that come from our throat, but longing for Him with ardent desires. And since a person asks a question in order to learn something of what he does not know, for a man to ask God means to realize that he is ignorant in God's sight. And God's answer is to teach His secret revelations to those who in humility know their ignorance...

42.3.6.en: Job himself was asking God through his longings and in humility, and he was seeking the answer from God by being taught through a revelation given in the words that follow. Job declared that he wanted to put a question, and yet he put nothing in the form of a question.

42.4.0.en: 5 I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee. 6 Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.

42.4.1.en: I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee [5].

42.4.2.en: Job confesses that what he formerly knew about God was through hearing of Him, so his knowledge of Him was vague and dark. But now he sees Him and enjoys His splendor, and so receives direct knowledge through vision. His knowledge of Him has become clear and radiant through the illumination of his inner eyes.

42.4.3.en: Job confesses that the answer came to him otherwise than he expected. Perhaps he was waiting for God to reveal to him through a vision or a dream the reason for what had befallen him, so that his heart might find rest. Perhaps he was waiting for God to tell him that what had befallen him was not comparable to what He was preparing for him in the age to come. But that God should appear to him and be manifested before him, and speak with him, this he could never have imagined.

42.4.4.en: Truly, the vision of God, whether with the heart through faith or face to face on the great day of the Lord, is a surpassing reward! The utmost that man desires is to see God.

42.4.5.en: * By these words he declares with very clear assurance that just as sight is higher than hearing, so too the progress he had come to through suffering made him different from his former state. And as he saw the light of truth with the inner eye more clearly, he came to distinguish plainly and to see the darkness of his humanity.

42.5.0.en: Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes [6].

42.5.1.en: When Job saw the Lord, he discovered also that he himself was sinful and unclean, as happened later with Isaiah, who, when he saw the Lord with His train filling the temple, realized that he was a man of unclean lips (Isa 6:5). In defending himself before his friends he often counted himself righteous, comparing himself with the people around him. But now he despised himself before God's holiness, righteousness and majesty. This is what St. Peter the Apostle did when the Lord performed a miracle and the Apostle perceived His divinity, and cried out: [Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord] (Lk 5:8).

42.5.2.en: In vain the friends strove with all their effort to convince Job that he was a great sinner; but the presence of God moved Job to repent with all his heart, in humility and contrition.

42.5.3.en: * The less a person is able to see himself, the less he is able to be displeased with himself. And the more he discerns the great light of grace, the more he realizes that he is to blame... For a man to repent in dust and ashes after contemplating the Supreme Being is for him to know that he is nothing but dust and ashes. Therefore the Lord says in the Gospel of the ungrateful city: “For if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes” (Mt 11:21). For sackcloth declares the roughness of sin and its pricks, while ashes are the dust of the dead. For this reason both are commonly used in repentance, that through the pricks of sackcloth we may know what we do through sin, and through being in the dust of ashes we may realize what we have come to through the sentence.

42.5.5.en: * With the eye of faith they look to the righteousness of God, and so they do not long to establish their own righteousness. They despise themselves, as Job says, and are dissolved, and count themselves dust and ashes (Job 42:6). This is what the phrase means: [they return to their dust]; but when they receive the Spirit of God they say: [I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me] (Gal 2:20). Thus the face of the earth is renewed by the whole company of the saints through the grace of the New Testament.

42.5.6.en: * The eye will have a lofty and wide-ranging power. Not the power of keen sight, such as is ascribed to serpents and eagles, which, however keen their sight, can distinguish only material things, and have no power to see what is not bodily. This great power of seeing may have been granted to the eyes of St. Job while he was still in the mortal body, when he said to God: “I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee. Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes” (Job 42:5-6). Yet there is no reason why we should refuse to understand this of the eye of the heart, of which the Apostle says: [The eyes of your understanding being enlightened] (Eph 1:18). That God will be seen with these eyes, no Christian doubts, who by faith accepts that our God and Lord says: “Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God” (Mt 5:8); but our question is whether we shall also see God in the life to come with the bodily eye?

42.6.0.en: And it was so, that after the LORD had spoken these words unto Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite,

42.6.1.en: My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends: for ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath [7].

42.6.2.en: Since Job was suffering under the weight of pains, what he said about God is counted far better than what his friends said, who were untried and not suffering. Perhaps some improper words came from Job, but God was hearing the words of his heart, his sighs and his hidden cries, and so counted him more righteous than they.

42.6.3.en: The Lord declared to Eliphaz, the eldest of the friends and the wisest, that their judgment on Job was mistaken, with nothing right in it, because they were unable to grasp the truth about the righteous Job. Their condemnation of their brother brought divine wrath upon them.

42.6.4.en: By outward appearance Job seemed to be murmuring against the divine judgment while his friends defended God's judgments. But in the language of the heart Job was justified before God, while they were condemned.

42.6.5.en: * God continues to call Job His servant, to indicate that He has wiped out all that had passed concerning him. Job spoke truly when he spoke about his good works, but you, by condemning him, did not speak what is right.

42.6.6.en: St. John Chrysostom * Job was preferred in the divine judgment over those who were defending the divine judgment...

42.6.7.en: By referring to Job as “servant,” God indicated that in all his defense Job did not speak with lofty pride, but with humble truth.

42.7.0.en: 8 Therefore take unto you now seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you: for him will I accept: lest I deal with you after your folly, in that ye have not spoken of me the thing which is right, like my servant Job. 9 So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did according as the LORD commanded them: the LORD also accepted Job.

42.7.1.en: Therefore take unto you now seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you: for him will I accept: lest I deal with you after your folly, in that ye have not spoken of me the thing which is right, like my servant Job [8].

42.7.2.en: The Lord's marvelous dealing astonishes man! Though He reproved Job in His personal talk with him, and showed him his inability to comprehend God's power, wisdom and plan, yet before the friends who opposed Job He glorifies him. He counts him an intercessor for them before Him.

42.7.3.en: This is the Lord's good pleasure, to glorify His believers and lift them up before their brethren as before the heavenly ones, and to bring them into the divine embrace.

42.7.4.en: The number 7 was regarded as a symbol of perfection, and so it was a general number in offering animal sacrifices (Lev 23:18; Num 29:32). Even among non-Jews we find Balaam asking Balak, king of Moab, to prepare this number of sacrifices (Num 23:1, 29).

42.7.5.en: The friends were unable to offer consolation to their friend amid the severity of his trials; but Job was vindicated by his endurance of the trials, not only to be justified in his friends' eyes, but, while still in the midst of affliction, before his body was healed and his temporal possessions restored and he enjoyed children, he was able to intercede before God for his friends who had almost crushed him!

42.7.6.en: Job's friends thought they were able to set Job right by their wisdom and human philosophy, and now the Lord assures them that they need Job to set their lives right by prayer.

42.7.7.en: * God used Job's friends to give testimony to a personal virtue. In the same way He showed the gravity of their error by using this exceptional means of offering sacrifice. For there would have been no call for these enormous sacrifices if the sin that required them had not been grave. He also made clear that the sacrifice alone is not sufficient, for He says, for his sake I did not want to excuse you from your sin. By this too He showed that He forgives them for his sake... By this we learn that accusing a righteous man is not a light sin that can be atoned for lightly.

42.7.8.en: * Prayers (those of others on our behalf) are of great benefit when we also contribute from our side. Do you want to know how great the benefit of prayers is? I say, consider Cornelius and Tabitha (Acts 10:3-4; 9:40). Hear also Jacob saying to Laban: [Except the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the fear of Isaac, had been with me, surely thou hadst sent me away now empty] (Gen 42:31). Hear also God saying: “For I will defend this city to save it, for mine own sake, and for my servant David's sake” (2 Kgs 6:20). But when? In the days of Hezekiah, who was righteous. So if prayers avail even for the exceedingly wicked, why did God not say this when Nebuchadnezzar came, and why did He deliver up the city? Because the evil prevailed all the more. Samuel himself too prayed for the Israelites and prevailed. But when? When they also were pleasing God, then they fought the enemies. You say: And what need is there of another's prayer if I myself please God? Do not say this, O man. Yes, there is need, and need of more prayer. Hear God saying of Job's friends: [My servant Job shall pray for you, and your sins shall be forgiven] (cf. Job 8:42). Indeed they had sinned, but not with a great sin. Yet this righteous man rescued his friends by prayer, at a time when the Jews were unable to rescue the perishing. They had learned this; hear God saying through the prophet: [Though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters] (cf. Ezek 14:14, 16). For evil had prevailed. Again: “Though Moses and Samuel stood before me...” (Jer 1:15). See, this was said of the prophets, because both prayed for them, and did not prevail.

42.7.9.en: St. John Chrysostom * Behold the just and merciful God, for He did not leave their errors without rebuking them, nor leave their offense without guidance. For He is our inner Physician; He first shows the corruption of our wound, and afterward points to the remedy for obtaining health. We have already said that the friends of the blessed Job represent the heretics, who oppose God while trying to defend Him. For by their words they rise up against the truth while thinking that they serve it by their false claims.

42.7.10.en: It must be noticed that they were commanded to offer a sacrifice to the Lord for their conversion, not to offer it by themselves, but through Job. Without doubt, when heretics turn back from their error, they cannot appease God's wrath toward them by offering a sacrifice by themselves... unless they return to the Church, which Job signifies... It is as though God says plainly to the heretics: I do not accept your sacrifices. I do not listen to the words of your supplications except through the intercession of the Church, whose words of confession concerning Me are true... Through her alone God accepts the sacrifice, and she alone intercedes with confidence for those who sin.

42.7.12.en: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did according as the LORD commanded them.

42.8.1.en: [The Lord accepted Job], that is, He accepted his prayers and offerings on behalf of his friends.

42.8.2.en: The wise man says: “Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof” (Eccl 7:8). The Lord did not prevent Satan from tempting Job, nor did He prevent Job's wife and friends from opposing him, mocking him and accusing him unjustly; but in due time He lifted up his face before the whole world, and his face has remained lifted up through the generations, and He will lift it up all the more on the great day of the Lord.

42.8.3.en: He did not send him an angel, nor an archangel, nor a cherub or seraph to comfort him and reassure him; rather the Lord Himself came down to lift up his face.

42.8.4.en: * When Job lost all his wealth, and when he lost his sons, all things seemed to work against him (Job 1:13-21); but since he loved the Lord, all the evils that befell him worked together for his good (Job 42:9-17). The sores of his body prepared him for the crown of heaven. Before the time of the trial God never spoke with him; but after the trial God came to him and spoke with him in friendship, as a friend with his friend. Let the calamity come, let every disaster come, so long as Christ is coming after the calamity.

42.8.5.en: St. Jerome It is fitting for us to look closely at the phrase: “the LORD accepted Job” (lit. lifted up Job's face). Since God forgave his friends for the sake of his prayers for them, God counted this gift as given to Job himself. Job's heart was simple and made wide by love even for his opponents, so the prayer for them went forth as though it concerned himself, for they were the object of his love!

42.8.6.en: * It is fitting to observe that the pardon they received was granted with such care, as the Lord declared, for the Lord did not lift up their faces but the face of the blessed Job.

42.9.0.en: 10 And the LORD turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before. 11 Then came there unto him all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all they that had been of his acquaintance before, and did eat bread with him in his house: and they bemoaned him, and comforted him over all the evil that the LORD had brought upon him: every man also gave him a piece of money, and every one an earring of gold. 12 So the LORD blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning: for he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses.

42.9.1.en: And the LORD turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before [10].

42.9.2.en: This expression is used when a person recovers his position and his means, so that he is like one freed from captivity who has returned to his land to live his life in freedom and dignity.

42.9.3.en: This does not mean that he suddenly received double what he had owned; it may have been accomplished gradually.

42.9.4.en: It is not strange that it is said of Job: “The LORD turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends.” For he enjoyed inward freedom when he lifted up his heart and mind, as well as his hands, on behalf of his opponents that God might pardon them. There is no way to enjoy freedom except by opening our hearts with love, not only to our loved ones and relatives, but even to our opponents and persecutors.

42.9.5.en: Since Job endured the trials without blaspheming God, but was occupied with the Kingdom of God, he received a double reward even in this world. The Lord Christ says: “Verily I say unto you, There is no man that hath left house, or parents, or brethren, or wife, or children, for the kingdom of God's sake, who shall not receive manifold more in this present time, and in the world to come life everlasting” (Lk 18:29-30).

42.9.6.en: God, who does not forget the one who gives a cup of cold water, will surely repay us manifold for what we offer, in one way or another, in this world as in the present world. He may not grant us material rewards, but in the midst of affliction He gives us inward joy, heavenly peace, divine consolations, satisfaction of the soul, and lasting happiness!

42.9.7.en: “The LORD turned the captivity of Job”: an Eastern expression meaning that the Lord restored to him his former prosperity. They regarded one who had lost his success and his goods as being in captivity or prison and wishing to be freed from it. The psalmist says: [Bring my soul out of prison, that I may praise thy name] (Ps 142:7).

42.9.8.en: St. John Chrysostom sees that God honored His servant Job by changing the nature of the earth, so that it produced for him double fruits contrary to custom. Thus God changes the laws of nature to honor those who honor Him.

42.9.9.en: [The lions knew Daniel and were restrained. The Son of Man came to us, and we were not restrained!

42.9.10.en: The lions preferred to die of hunger rather than touch the body of the saint, while we see Christ stripped and dying of hunger (in His brethren) and we do not give them what is surplus to us, but live in luxury and ignore the saints. Again the earth gave to another friend of God (Job) so many gifts from its bowels, and produced a harvest such as had never been before.]

42.9.11.en: * Do you not see what it means to lose something for God's sake? It means that you receive it back doubled. The Gospels promise you even more: “an hundredfold,” besides eternal life (Mt 19:29) in Christ Jesus.

42.9.12.en: Origen * He made his prayers more effective for his own account when he offered them for the benefit of others. For the sacrifice of prayer is accepted all the more in the eyes of the merciful Judge when it carries the breath of love for one's neighbor. And a person adds to its effectiveness if he offers it for his enemies. For the Truth, who is our Teacher, says: “Pray for them which despitefully use you” (Lk 6:28). Again He says: “And when ye stand praying, forgive, if ye have ought against any: that your Father also which is in heaven may forgive you your trespasses” (Mk 11:25).

42.9.13.en: * It was said to Judah in his suffering: “For a small moment have I forsaken thee; but with great mercies will I gather thee” (Isa 54:7)... For the one who was struck by God's permission also suffered by the words of his friends, and when he was comforted by the gifts of divine mercy he was also made worthy to be comforted by human love, so that just as the pains and troubles of suffering wounded him from both sides, so the joys of consolations meet him from every side.

42.9.15.en: * (The Apostle Paul) had read that Abraham, when he confessed that he was dust and ashes, found God's grace in his deep humility (Gen 18:27). And he read that Job, when he sat on his dunghill, recovered all his losses (Job 2:8; 42:10-17), and he read David's prophecy: [He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, and lifteth the needy out of the dunghill] (Ps 113:7).

42.9.16.en: St. Ambrose * As I said, many called upon God and were rescued at once, without waiting for the life to come. Job, as an example, was delivered over to Satan at his own request, afflicted and full of worms, yet in this life he received his health and recovered double what he had lost. Whereas the Lord was scourged and no one was found to help Him.

42.9.17.en: St. Augustine What Job enjoyed bears the image or symbol of what we enjoy in Christ Jesus, in whom our captivity was turned back, we who had enslaved ourselves to the devil, and He gave us double glories.

42.10.0.en: Then came there unto him all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all they that had been of his acquaintance before, and did eat bread with him in his house: and they bemoaned him, and comforted him over all the evil that the LORD had brought upon him: every man also gave him a piece of money, and every one an earring of gold [11].

42.10.1.en: His friends and acquaintances showed that their opposition to him had been out of ignorance, for when the Lord directed them to the truth they submitted from the whole heart with sincerity, confessed their error, and came with gifts for Job, the man of God.

42.10.2.en: It is clear from this text that his brothers and sisters did not come to him throughout the period of his trial, which made the trial more bitter. For even those nearest to him did not approach him to comfort and help him (cf. Job 19:13-14).

42.10.3.en: Each one gave him a piece of silver; in the Septuagint it reads “each gave a lamb.”

42.10.4.en: It was an ancient custom for friends to give gifts to one who had come out of affliction, as happened with Hezekiah (2 Chr 32:23).

42.10.5.en: In some regions of the East even now, when a man falls into affliction his friends and relatives visit him and bring him gifts to compensate him for what he has lost and to support him in his affliction, and as an expression of their longing for his return to his former prosperity.

42.10.6.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that Job's brothers and sisters, who made light of Job during his ordeal and returned to him with gifts when the Lord turned his captivity, point to the Jews who made light of the Lord Christ at His passion and crucifixion and did not believe; for when Elijah comes in the last days he will bring all back to Him (Rom 11:25-26).

42.10.7.en: So the LORD blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning.

42.11.0.en: For he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses [12].

42.11.1.en: In great brevity the book is concluded by the turning of the burning fire of trial into a fire of heavenly glory. This is the wonderful mystery of suffering! It is the mystery of true glory.

42.12.0.en: 13 He had also seven sons and three daughters. 14 And he called the name of the first, Jemima; and the name of the second, Kezia; and the name of the third, Keren-happuch. 15 And in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job: and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.

42.12.1.en: He had also seven sons and three daughters [13].

42.12.2.en: The last time his wife is mentioned is in Job 19:17, where Job groans that his breath was strange to her. This has led some to believe that Job's sons and daughters were from a second wife (perhaps after the death of the first).

42.12.3.en: Origen sees that the sons and daughters point to God's gifts to the believer; the sons are a symbol of the good works of the spirit, and the daughters the holy works of the body in the Lord. The birth of sons and daughters points to the work of God's Spirit, who sanctifies spirit and body, so that the believer bears the fruits of the Spirit in his whole being.

42.12.4.en: On the great day of the Lord Job will stand before the Lord saying:

42.12.5.en: [Behold, I and the children which the LORD hath given me](a). So it is fitting for every believer to be fruitful, never ceasing to beget, in the Lord, holy children.

42.13.0.en: And he called the name of the first, Jemima; and the name of the second, Kezia; and the name of the third, Keren-happuch [14].

42.13.1.en: The names of the daughters are mentioned here to express the atmosphere of happiness and joy that prevailed in the family:

42.13.2.en: יְמִימָה “Jemima,” appears in the Septuagint as Heameram and means a day, so her beauty was like the light of day. The following note appears in the Chaldean version: “He gave her the name Jemima, because her beauty is like the day.” The Septuagint, the Vulgate and the Chaldean noted that “Jemima” is derived from the Hebrew word יוֹם “day, Yowm.” For Job has passed from the night of trials to the day of joy. The light has shone on his tent.

42.13.3.en: The following note appears in the Chaldean: “She was precious like cassia.” Cassia is mentioned in Ps 45:8 among the precious perfumes.

42.13.4.en: The third bears the name of a paint used for the eye-lashes so that the eye appears wider and more beautiful, since wide eyes are one of the marks of beauty in the East.

42.14.0.en: Rosenmuller, in his comment on this passage, says that a Jewish writer called Solomon Jarichi observes that the names of Job's daughters point to their beauty, as stated in [15]. The first name, Jemima, represents a clear day carrying the splendor of its beauty. According to Hesychius it means a day, and is a figure for Diana. The second name, Kezia, means Cassia, one of the most precious of the ancient perfumes. The third name, Keren-happuch, means a horn of eye-paint, which gives beauty to the eye. In other words, it is a vessel made of horn in which Eastern women keep the substance for beautifying their eyes. Thomas Roe observed in his travels that the Persians were accustomed to give their women names meaning perfumes or spices or pearls or precious stones or anything beautiful and delightful.

42.14.1.en: Gesenius holds that Jemima is derived from the Arabic word “yamama,” a dove. And Dr. Alexander, in Kitto's Cyclopedia, defines Keren-happuch as the horn of adornment or beauty.

42.14.2.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa sees that the three daughters of Job were so named:

42.14.3.en: “Day,” and as the Apostle says, that we have become children of the day, living in purity (Eph 5:8).

42.14.4.en: Cassia, in which purity and a sweet fragrance appear.

42.14.5.en: The horn of Almatheia: it is related in the Greek accounts that there was an Almatheia who had a wild goat, and who was fond of the Cretan goat whose horn had fallen off, and from it flowed all kinds of fruits.

42.14.6.en: Pope Gregory sees that the human race passes through three stages: 1. The first stage, when man was created, so he was a day, like the first daughter. 2. The second stage, when man enjoys salvation and the fragrance of Christ rises from him, so that he becomes cassia. 3. The third stage, when we meet God face to face and share with the heavenly ones, so that we are counted like a musical instrument, the “horn.”

42.14.7.en: * What is the reason that Job's first daughter is called Day, the second Cassia and the third Keren-happuch, cornustibii, except that the whole human race, chosen by the tenderness of its Creator and by the mercy of the Savior Himself, is indicated by these names?... The human race shines in splendor upon creation with the light of innocence. Then, when they are saved, a sweet fragrance goes out from them by the practice of good works. For this reason the first daughter was called Day and the second, not without fitness, Cassia. Cassia is rightly so named, since the fragrance of the exalted life rises from her strongly. And it was also said by the prophet of the Savior Himself at His coming: “All thy garments smell of myrrh, and aloes, and cassia, out of the ivory palaces, whereby they have made thee glad” (Ps 45:8)... But because the human race, in its third state, even when it is formed anew for the resurrection of the body, is engaged in the harmony of the eternal praise, the third daughter is called “Keren-happuch.” What does cornustibii mean but the song of those who rejoice? For truly what is said by the prophet is fulfilled: [Sing unto the LORD a new song] (Ps 149:1). It is truly fulfilled when the song of praise is sung to God, no longer by faith but by contemplation of the One who made the human race a day by creating it, and cassia by offering it salvation, and Keren-happuch by possessing it. For we who were light when we were created have now become cassia by our salvation, and at last we shall become Keren-happuch when we are engaged in the eternal praise.

42.14.9.en: And in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job.

42.14.10.en: And their father gave them inheritance among their brethren [15].

42.14.11.en: Among the Jews a daughter inherited from her parents when she had no brother born (Num 27:8).

42.14.12.en: * The souls of the elect surpass in their dazzling beauty the whole human race that is on the earth.

42.14.13.en: * When our compassionate Savior comes, no one will ever despair, because of his weakness, of obtaining the heavenly inheritance. For our Father gives women also the right of inheritance with the males, and so gathers the weak and the humble with the strong and the perfect, that all may have a share in the heavenly inheritance. The Truth Himself says in the Gospel: “In my Father's house are many mansions” (Jn 14:2).

42.15.0.en: 16 After this lived Job an hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons' sons, even four generations. 17 So Job died, being old and full of days.

42.15.1.en: After this lived Job an hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons' sons, even four generations [16].

42.15.2.en: According to the Septuagint translation Job lived 170 years after the trial, so all the days of his life were 240 years, that is, the trial came upon him at the age of seventy.

42.15.3.en: Seeing one's grandchildren was a sign of the blessing granted to the godly, as stated in Ps 128:6.

42.16.0.en: So Job died, being old and full of days [17].

42.16.1.en: Job experienced in his life how to live with God as the greatest of the men of the East at that time, and how to live in the midst of bitter pains, sitting on the dunghill covered with worms, attacked by his friends, with not even his nearest kin asking after him. He tasted grief, poverty and affliction as no one had experienced before him or after him. He tasted a life of prosperity and a life of bitterness, as though in his life he had witnessed God's care for man in every circumstance.

42.16.2.en: That I may see You amid the furnace of trials

42.16.3.en: * You testified of Job that he was righteous and upright, the best of all the people of his time, yet he did not enjoy the sight of You except in the furnace of trials.

42.16.4.en: I confess to You my weaknesses and my sins.

42.16.5.en: In Your love for me You have allowed me bitter afflictions, for You desire to reveal Yourself to me; I see You and rejoice in You.

42.16.6.en: * The consolations of men often increase my pains.

42.16.7.en: There is none who can share my pains except You.

42.16.8.en: Your words enter my heart like arrows, wounding me with wounds of surpassing love.

42.16.9.en: I discover my reality as dust and ashes, and I realize that You raise a heaven out of my dust, and instead of ashes my heart becomes a holy temple for You.

42.16.10.en: * Your words prepare me to see You with the eyes of my heart.

42.16.11.en: Then my soul rejoices with the wounded Job, saying:

42.16.12.en: I have heard of You by the hearing of the ear, but now my eyes see You!

42.16.13.en: * Grant me, with the tried Job, to open my heart to those who mock me.

42.16.14.en: Let me not cease to pray for them with sincere love.

42.16.15.en: Let my soul even be broken before You, so that the whole world may enjoy the sight of You, and share with me Your surpassing gifts.

42.16.16.en: * You gave Job seven sons and three daughters; grant me to be a father to many.

42.16.17.en: Wherever I am found, let Your Spirit work to draw many to You!

42.16.18.en: My soul will not rest until I see the whole world as Your sons and daughters!

42.16.19.en: * Grant me a holy old age, a spiritual fruit for each day of my sojourn, counted in Your eyes as a thousand years according to Your divine promise!
